title: Introduce modular spacing rhythm and shadow translation for compact tables
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need to standardize a compact spacing rhythm and a deterministic shadow/elevation translation for data tables, inline cards, and primary/secondary buttons. Current implementation contains multiple ad-hoc spacing values (8px/10px/12px mixtures) and inconsistent shadow levels that cause visual jitter at high density. This ticket scopes audit, spec, and handoff for a small, modular spacing scale (micro, tight, base, stack) and a translation matrix that maps legacy elevation tokens to new semantic elevation tokens (surface-e1..e4).

Objectives:
- Audit current token usage across Tables, Buttons, Cards, and Form controls. Identify where ad-hoc spacing/radius/shadow values are used.
- Define a 4-step modular spacing rhythm optimized for dense UIs: micro (4), tight (6), base (8), stack (12) — numbers are px but tokens are named semantic (spacing.micro, spacing.tight, spacing.base, spacing.stack).
- Create a complementary radius scale: radius.micro (2), radius.small (4), radius.medium (6). Prioritize radius.medium for interactive controls and radius.small for table cells at compact density.
- Define shadow/elevation translation: produce a matrix that maps legacy shadow tokens (e.g., shadow-1, shadow-2) to semantic elevations surface-e1..e4 with exact CSS box-shadow formulas and a CSS variable set for color/alpha. Include disabled/pressed variants.
- Accessibility & contrast: ensure spacing changes do not reduce hit targets below WCAG guidance; document any exceptions and reasoned mitigations (e.g., increased line-height vs. width).
- Produce a migration guide and automated codemod list for engineering to replace ad-hoc values with tokens.

Scope out of this ticket:
- Global color palette redesign (covered in a separate ticket).
- Full rollout to mobile-specific breakpoints (follow-up ticket will adapt tokens for mobile scaling).

Deliverables:
- Figma token page with new spacing and radius scales plus component examples for compact table row, dense card, primary/secondary button states.
- Design token spec doc (Confluence) detailing token names, px mappings, CSS variables, and rationales.
- Migration checklist and example codemods for web repo.
- A minimal set of unit visual regression shots for Table, Button, and Card in compact density.

Acceptance criteria:
- All examples in Figma updated and approved by Design Lead.
- Confluence spec published with explicit mapping from legacy token names to new semantic tokens.
- Engineering PR created that replaces at least 70% of ad-hoc spacing in the tables package and introduces CSS variables for surface-e1..e4.
- No interactive control violates 44x44px target without documented exception.

Notes on trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Chose a 4-step spacing system instead of a 6-step system to reduce cognitive overhead for developers working on dense interfaces. This increases reuse but may require small visual compromises in some edge-case layouts.
- Shadow translation favors lower alpha flat shadows for tables to avoid perceived depth collapse when rows stack; the card tokens keep slightly higher spread.

Rollout plan and risks:
- Week 1 (this ticket): finalize tokens and spec; update Figma.
- Week 2: partner with ENG to land the CSS variable scaffolding and a first-pass codemod.
- Week 3: design QA and visual regression sweep; iterate based on results.
- Risk: small layout regressions in legacy pages. Mitigation: codemod + feature-flagged rollout and quick rollback PR template.
